headline: Deadlocked reaches 10.21% matched code with network and cross-game work
summary: Deadlocked's NTSC-U v1.00 matched code rose from 9.52% to 10.21% in the project's progress report. A matched function compiles to exactly the same bytes as the original game. That report lists 7,163 of 18,170 functions. The day's separate map tally instead records 7,177 NTSC-U functions and 7,756 of 18,134 PAL functions.
highlights: Network, menu and level routines landed in #119 and #124, including converting existing near misses into exact matches.
#122 and #125 adapt routines already matched in Going Commando and Up Your Arsenal, covering both NTSC-U and PAL.
PAL-specific work includes menu and object-setup routines (#115, #117, #120, #126). #120 leaves NTSC-U progress unchanged.
OpenRAC's local changes are upstream, allowing its Deadlocked submodule to use main without local patches (#127).
Draft #121 and new batches #128, #129, #130, #131, #132 and #133 remained unmerged.
#134 reports audit failures involving trailing fill words and PAL objects in the US relocation audit. Its author kept the affected functions out of the pull requests.
